question: Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2, & x \leq 2 \\ 4x - 4, & x > 2 \end{cases}$. Is $f(x)$ continuous and differentiable at $x=2$?
explanation:
Left limit at $x=2$: $\lim_{x\to 2^-} x^2 = 4$

Right limit at $x=2$: $\lim_{x\to 2^+} 4x - 4 = 4$

$f(2) = 4$, so function is continuous at $x=2$.

Left derivative at $x=2$: derivative of $x^2$ is $2x$, so value is $4$.

Right derivative at $x=2$: derivative of $4x - 4$ is $4$.

Both derivatives are equal, so differentiable.

Hence, option A.
